samples: This program models a traffic light as a state machine: given the current colour (red, green, yellow or flashing red) and an event (timer expiry, emergency declared, emergency cleared), it computes the next colour. Timer events cycle red to green to yellow and back to red, an emergency forces flashing red that ignores timers, and clearing the emergency returns to red. It also can replay a list of events from a starting colour to give the sequence of lights shown, and its `main` just prints one demo run (starting at red, with an emergency in the middle) to the console, so it is a small, pure, easily reusable logic piece with only the demo needing console access.

This program models a traffic light as a small state machine: given the current colour (red, green, yellow, or flashing red) and an event (timer expiry, emergency declared, or emergency cleared), it works out the next colour, with an emergency forcing flashing red until it is cleared and the light returns to red. It can also apply a whole list of events in order and return the light shown after each one. The built-in demo starts at red, runs a short sequence with an emergency in the middle, and prints each resulting colour to the console, so it needs only console access and has no other side effects.

This program models a traffic light as a state machine: given the current colour (red, green, yellow, or flashing red) and an event (timer expired, emergency declared, or emergency cleared), it returns the next colour, cycling normally on timer events while an emergency forces flashing red until it is cleared and the light returns to red. It can also apply a whole list of events in order and report the light shown after each one. Running it prints a built-in demo sequence of five events, including one emergency, to the console, and it needs no other permissions (no network or file access).

This program models a traffic light as a state machine. It cycles Red, Green, Yellow, Red on timer events, switches to a flashing red when an emergency is declared (staying there on timer ticks), and returns to Red when the emergency is cleared. It can also replay a list of events from a starting light to give the resulting sequence of lights, and its entry point prints the results of a built-in demo sequence with one emergency in the middle. It is pure logic apart from console output, so it is easy to reuse as a small library, but the demo is fixed and takes no input.

This program models a traffic light as a state machine: given the current colour (red, green, yellow, or flashing red) and an event (timer expired, emergency declared, or emergency cleared), it works out the next colour. Timer events move the light through the normal red, green, yellow cycle, while an emergency forces it to flashing red and clearing the emergency returns it to red. It also offers a helper that applies a list of events in order and returns the resulting lights, and its main routine prints the results for a short demo sequence with one emergency, needing only console output and no other permissions.
